en: Advayavajra’s Works 12. *Svapnanirukti*,
edited by Mahāmahopādhyāya Hara Prasad Shastri.
In *Advayavajrasaṃgraha*, GOS 1927, Baroda;
edited by the Mikkyō Seiten Kenkyūkai;
and in the *Taishō Daigaku Sōgō Bukkyō Kenkyūjo Nenpō*.
Homage to the Omniscient One.
In the Vinaya, the Abhidharma, and the Sūtras, the preeminent Conquerors have declared that all phenomena are like a dream; this is now being explained with clarity. (1)
Is a dream real or unreal? Is it a manifold of consciousness, or is it consciousness itself? Is it illusion, or is it without foundation? What is agreed upon here by the wise? (2)
A dream is real through ignorance; upon awakening, it becomes unreal. In the first case there is the notion of permanence; in the second, non-existence would occur. (3)
Upon the awakening [of wisdom] and the removal of what is imagined, experience itself is not negated;
for there exists the great experience whose nature is the manifold manifestation of being, consciousness, and light. (4)
From the fundamental store-consciousness (*ālayavijñāna*), which perishes moment by moment, there arise various forms of active consciousnesses;
these, appearing as its own images therein, are held to be nothing other than consciousness itself. (5)
When one dream arises from another dream, then consciousness is like a painted picture;
it is neither real because it is known to be unreal, nor is there annihilation because it is manifest.
Is a name applied where there is no name, or is it applied to a name that is itself an illusion?
A name is not applicable to a name, nor does establishment exist in the nameless.
In this [context], among the six, two are to be abandoned and four are considered conducive to awakening.
Thus has this entire universe been described as being like a dream by the Supreme Victors. (8)

Furthermore, know that the supreme essence of all the Buddhas is found not through intellectual speculation, but through the realization of the true guru, through diligent effort, and especially through spiritual conduct. (9)
The Exposition of Dreams is completed.
Farewell.
